Q1: The British. A Union Jack flies over the stone tower and walls of the town on the Rock in frames 40–41 (Jan 1780). The pictures don't show how or when they got it.
Q2: "1779 — The Great Siege" (the caption in frame 23). Camps and trench lines appear on the land side, and ships gather in the bay.
Q3: Not sure. The pictures never show hunger directly. A blockade seems to be the cause: camps and a trench line on land, and ships sitting off the town. I saw no food, no starving people and no text about hunger.
Q4: A relief fleet of ships. A group of sailing ships arrives in the bay on 18 Jan 1780 (frame 47), and people unload supplies on the quay or mole in frames 48–49 (22 and 26 Jan 1780). The pictures don't say who they are or exactly what they bring. A different, larger fleet of ships sits offshore in April 1781 (frames 53–59), and it could be a relief fleet or an attacker.
